author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: A television tie-in collection gathering the short stories that seeded the 2017-18 anthology series Electric Dreams, showcasing PKD's obsessions with android empathy, precognition, and worlds that quietly refuse to hold still.
page_summary:
Electric Dreams collects the Philip K. Dick short stories adapted for the Channel 4 / Amazon anthology series of the same name. It pulls tales from across his 1950s magazine period, when Dick wrote fast for pulp markets and used the constraints of the short form to test single, sharp premises: a machine that predicts crime, a colonist who cannot trust his own perceptions, a small clerk crushed between vast impersonal systems.

The collection matters as a demonstration of how durable those premises are. Stories written for disposable magazines were mined decades later by screenwriters because their engines still turn: paranoia, precognition, the android that may be more human than its owner, the reality that peels away to show something underneath. The book lets a reader see the raw material before television reshaped it.

For the QueryPat archive, this entry marks the point where Dick's early stories cross into contemporary adaptation, and where his mid-century anxieties get reread as commentary on surveillance, automation, and manufactured experience.
